subject: sg-succession
note: Sweep over three Singapore Acts. The publisher (SSO) exposes a per-Act version timeline rather than the UK-style F-marker apparatus, so the annotation inventory in the source bundle is the set of dated versions and the dispositions below join on it.

searches.question: Has any Singapore court struck down, stayed or read down a provision of the ISA, the Wills Act or the PAA?
searches.scope: lawplain judgments corpus (SGCA/SGHC/SGDC), full text, all years
searches.query: Intestate Succession Act section 7 distribution per stirpes
searches.coverage_note: Does NOT cover: unreported decisions; Syariah Court rulings (which is where a Muslim estate would be decided, and which this encoding routes to rather than modelling); decisions turning on the Wills Act's formal-validity sections, which were not separately searched.

searches.question: Is any amendment to these Acts enacted but not yet reflected, or formally proposed?
searches.scope: sso.agc.gov.sg landing page version timeline for ISA1967, WA1838, PAA1934
searches.coverage_note: Captures what SSO PUBLISHES as versions. Does NOT cover Bills before Parliament that SSO has not yet published, nor commencement notices for enacted-but-unbrought-into-force provisions.

searches.question: Is reform of intestate succession -- in particular the exclusion of illegitimate children -- pending?
searches.query: Singapore Intestate Succession Act amendment 2024 2025 2026 reform illegitimate children
searches.coverage_note: Open-web search only. Does NOT cover the Government Gazette, Parliamentary Hansard, or Law Reform Committee papers, none of which were searched. A negative result here is weak evidence of no reform, and is recorded as a currency risk rather than as an all-clear.

entries.summary: Lim Weipin v Lim Boh Chuan [2010] SGHC 99 applies ISA s 3's definition of 'child' -- 'a legitimate child and includes any child adopted by virtue of an order of court' -- as the gate on who may claim under s 7 rule 3. The court treated the definition as decisive of standing, litigating adoption on the facts.

provenance.citation: Lim Weipin and another v Lim Boh Chuan and others [2010] SGHC 99
provenance.quote: "child" means a legitimate child and includes any child adopted by virtue of an order of court

entries.disposition_note: Settles fork F2 in favour of the narrow reading: membership of the `children` list is a legitimacy/adoption question decided before the rules run. The encoding delegates it to the fact supplier and says so, rather than silently admitting every biological child.

entries.summary: Cheng Tze Tzuen v Dang Lan Anh [2025] SGHC 112: entitlement to letters of administration is based on priority of entitlement to the estate under s 7 of the ISA -- linking the PAA's grant question to the ISA's distribution order.

provenance.citation: Cheng Tze Tzuen v Dang Lan Anh [2025] SGHC 112
provenance.quote: Entitlement to the letters of administration is based on priority of entitlement to the estate under s 7 of the Intestate Succession Act 1967

entries.disposition_note: Corroborates encoding PAA s 18(4) against the ISA s 7 class order rather than as a free-standing list, which is how the PAA module is written.

entries.summary: The 2020 Revised Edition (in force 31 Dec 2021) restated all three Acts, and Act 24 of 2022 (wef 28/10/2022) extended Wills Act s 27(5)'s definition of 'soldier' to a serviceman serving in the digital and intelligence service of the Singapore Armed Forces.

provenance.citation: Wills Act 1838 s 27(5), as amended by Act 24 of 2022 wef 28/10/2022
provenance.quote: “soldier” includes a member of an air force and a serviceman serving in the digital and intelligence service of the Singapore Armed Forces

entries.disposition_note: Already present in the fetched current text and encoded from it. Disposed as SUBSUMED rather than as a dated arm because this corpus carries no rule-version axis: it states the law as at the bundle's in-force date, and this amendment is inside that date. A corpus that later gains dated arms should re-dispose this entry as `encoded` naming the arm.

entries.summary: Reform of the exclusion of illegitimate children from intestate succession is under public discussion, but no Bill, no formal proposal and no commencement notice was found.

provenance.url_absent_reason: No instrument exists to cite. The finding is the ABSENCE of a Bill or proposal, which is why it is routed as a currency risk rather than as a modification.
provenance.citation: no instrument found; public commentary only

routing.effective_from_absent_reason: Nothing has been enacted or formally proposed, so there is no date to record.

entries.disposition_note: CURRENCY RISK, UNDATED. If the exclusion is reformed, ISA s 3 changes and the `children` list's membership rule changes with it -- which would alter the answer for a large class of real users without altering a single rule in s 7. Flagged rather than encoded because there is nothing to encode: no instrument exists. Re-run S3 against Hansard and the Gazette before relying on this corpus for a death after 2026.

dispositions.note: The corpus encodes the CURRENT consolidated text (in force 18 Aug 2026) and does not carry dated arms on the rule-version axis.
